Annual revenue of Akbar's treasury in 1600 AD at £17.5 million (in contrast to the entire treasury of Great Britain two hundred years later in 1800 AD, which totalled £16 million).
India experienced unprecedented prosperity in history.
the Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India (1498), were also the last to leave this land (1961).
Third Anglo-Mysore War: Tipu Sultan had to pay Rs.3 Crore as war indemnity. He also had to surrender 2 of his sons as surety to the British till he paid his due.

rows.html: Scholars:
Romesh Chandra Dutt: In early 20th century ≈ £20 million flew out of India.
MG Ranade: In his book "Essay on Indian Economics," he claimed that Britishers drained more than one-third of India's wealth into England.
Dadabhai Naoroji: India's tax burden in 1886 was 14.3% of total revenue, significantly higher than England's 6.93%.
Angus Maddison (British economist): India's share of the world income went from 27% in 1700 AD (compared to Europe's share of 23%) to 3% in 1950.
Reports:
'Takers Not Makers: The Unjust Poverty and Unearned Wealth of Colonial Inheritance' report, 2025 (Oxfam):
Wealth Drain during Colonial Period -> Between 1765 and 1900, UK drained $64.82 trillion from India, with $33.8 trillion going to the top 10%.
India and its Contradictions: In the 18th century, India became a land of contrasts because extreme poverty and extreme luxury existed side by side.
Between 1730 to 1947 → 31 famines, loss of life of 8.5 cr. Indians
In 1770, there was a terrible Famine in Bengal which killed about 1 Crore people.
Permanent Settlement:
Covered 20% of British India
The state received 10/11th of the rent the zamindars received from the peasantry, with only 1/11th going to the zamindars themselves.
Between 1794 and 1819, 68% of zamindari land was sold in Bengal.
Ryotwari System:
Covered 51% area of British India.
Revenue was fixed at very high rate (45-50%)
Up until 1750, India produced about 25% of the world's industrial output.
India had a 25% share of the global textile trade in the early 18th century.
By 1664, the English East India Company imported more than 750,000 pieces of cotton goods from India, which accounted for 73 per cent of the Company’s total trade.
On April 16, 1853 -> first railway line in India spanning upto 34 kilometers between Boribandar (Bombay) to Thane.
Built 6000 kms of track by 1869 and 45,000 km of track by 1905 with the help of private enterprises.
Railway length = ~69,439 route km (~1.32 lakh track km) today (Economic Survey 2025-26) --> ~53,000–54,000 km built during British rule before 1947 (Ministry of Railways).

rows.html: Cornawallis Reforms:
all higher posts in administration worth more than 500 pounds a year in salary could be held by Englishmen only.
Charter Act of 1793 had reserved all posts worth 500 pounds per annum for the covenant servants of the Company.
Salary of the Collector of a district was raised to Rs. 1500 a month and 1 per cent commission on the revenue collected from his district.
Viscount Lee Commission recommendations (1924): Parity between Indians and Europeans: To be achieved 50:50 parity in 15 years.
Morley-Minto Reforms: number of members in the Central Legislative Council was raised from 16 to 60.
Provinces: 3 provinces in 1773 to 17 provinces in 1947.
Status of illiteracy: ~94% in 1911 (~6% literacy) and ~92% in 1921 (~8% literacy; ~84% illiteracy at Independence in 1947) (Census of British India / NCERT)
Number of Universities:
1857: 3 (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras)
1947: 19 universities, ~500 colleges
Age of Consent Act(1891): Raised age of consent for girls from 10 to 12 years.
Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929): Minimum marriage age: 14 (girls) and 18 (boys).
Gandhi ji campaign for untouchability: Gandhi’s campaign against untouchability which covered 12,500 miles and lasted for nine months.
Poona Pact: Number of seats reserved for the depressed classes in provincial legislatures would be increased from 71 in the Award to 147; and to 18% of the total in central legislature.
Rabindranath Tagore wrote around 2230 songs.

rows.html: European Soldier to Indian soldier ratio: 1:2
Revolt of 1857 -> Proportion of Europeans to Indians was carefully fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay Armies to avoid another revolt (Peel Commission, 1859 / NCERT).
In Awadh, more than 20,000 taluqdars had their estates confiscated
Reason given for Partition: Population of 78 million Bengal had become too big to be administered.
House of Lords endorsed Reginald Dyer’s action and the British public showed solidarity with him by helping collect 30,000 pounds for him for his atrocities in Jallianwala Bagh.
1st nationwide movement launched by Gandhiji in 1920 during British rule.
During Non-cooperation Movement:
Thousands of students left schools and colleges and joined only 800 national schools and colleges.
Rs 1 crore were raised for Tilak Swaraj Fund by August 1921, and 1 crore/50 lakhs members got enrolled in Congress.
Consequence of Non-Cooperation Movement: The import of foreign goods halved between 1921 and 1922.
Tilak’s Home Rule League had 6 Branches while Annie Besant’s Home rule League had 200+ Branches.
Gandhi along with a band of 78 members of Sabarmati Ashram, marched from his headquarters in Ahmedabad for 240 miles.
On April 23, 1930, the arrest of Congress leaders in the NWFP led to the participation of a 92% Muslim population.

Gandhi’s Eleven demands -> Reduce Rupee-Sterling Exchange Ratio to 1s 4d: Called for a change in the exchange rate between the Indian rupee and the British pound to benefit Indian traders and businesses.
1937 elections were held in 11 provinces- Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar, Orissa, Assam, NWFP, Bengal, Punjab, Bombay and Sindh

In 1937 elections, An estimated 30.1 million persons, including 4.25 million women, had acquired the right to vote (12% of the total population), and 15.5 millions of these, including 917,000 women, participated to exercise their franchise.
In 1937 elections, Among the 864 seats assigned “general” constituencies, Congress contested 739 and won 617.

Independence: 4%

Doubled till 1981

rows.html: Functional Jails: 1,333 jails | Sanctioned Capacity of Prisons: 4.53 lakh inmates (actual inmate population exceeded 5.11 lakh at the end of 2024, up from 4.25 lakh capacity in 2021) [NCRB Prison Statistics India 2024]
Occupancy Rate [Overcrowding]: 112.7% nationally in 2024 (Delhi highest at 194.6%, Meghalaya 163.5%, J&K 148.3%) [NCRB Prison Statistics India 2024] (>130% in earlier PSI / IJR 2025)
Undertrial: ~73% (72.6%) in 2024 (down from 77% peak in 2021; Delhi and Bihar >87%) (NCRB Prison Statistics India 2024) 76% in [India Justice Report 2025]
Funding for Prisons: avg daily spend per inmate is mere Rs 121 (IJR 2025)

blocks.title: Composition of Prisons [NCRB's Prison Statistics India - 2021]
Composition of Prisons [NCRB’s Prison Statistics India – 2021]

rows.html: Gender-wise: 4.3% are women prisoners.
Vulnerable Sections: Over 85% of prisoners are SC/ST/OBC/Muslims.
Psychologists: Only 25 psychologists for the entire prison population—an average of 1 for every 22,928 prisoners (Recommended: 1:500)
Doctors Availability: 1: 775 Prisoners vs 1:300 (Recommended) [IJR 2025]
Shortage of Staff: ~30–33% overall staff vacancy, with a 46.4% vacancy rate in sanctioned medical staff in 2024 (NCRB PSI 2024 / IJR 2025)
Lack of Child Centers: Nearly 18000 children are living in jails only because their parents are in jails.

rows.html: Social services expenditure (SSE): General government SSE rose to 7.9% of GDP in FY 2025-26 (BE), up from 7.7% in FY25 (RE) and 7.0% in FY24 (SSE as % of total expenditure rose from 23.3% in FY21 to 26.2% in FY25 BE) (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Healthcare Spending: India spent Rs 9.04 lakh crore on health in FY 2022 -> 3.8% of GDP or Rs 6,602/person at current prices (Eco. Survey)
National Health Mission (NHM): 5.23 lakh workers, including 1.38 lakh Community Health Officers. Certification of 7,998 public health facilities under National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS).
Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission: > 42 crore health records have been linked to ABHA.
Literacy Rate: 74.04% (2011 census)
77% (National Statistical Office (NSO)) -> nearly 8 out of 10 people can read and write.
Mid-Day Meal Scheme: covers about 11.80 crore children studying in 11.20 lakh schools across the country.
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM): Declared rural India Open Defecation Free (ODF) in October 2019.

Swachh Bharat Mission Phase II – Grameen (SBM-G): During April- Nov 2024, 1.92 lakh villages were incrementally declared ODF+ under model category, taking the total number of ODF+ villages to 3.64 lakh.
Cleanliness Ranking: Indore has distinguished itself by winning the overall cleanest city award for seven consecutive years
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): total DBT was ₹6.91 lakh crore in FY24
Public Distribution System (PDS): Covering around 800 million beneficiaries under the NFSA.
Saubhagya Scheme: Achieved 100% village electrification in 2018, and near-universal household electrification.

Renewable energy: total non-fossil fuel installed electricity capacity reached 283.46 GW (including 274.68 GW Renewable Energy: 150.26 GW Solar, 56.09 GW Wind, 51.41 GW Large Hydro) as of 31 March 2026, up from 203.18 GW (MNRE / CEA 2026)
Power consumption rises 7% to 148.48 bn units in March 2025
Solar-plus-storage systems in India can now deliver round-the-clock electricity at under ₹6/kWh, cheaper than coal.
Addition of 75.89% connections since the launch of the mission.

Households with tap water connections increased from 3.23 crore (17%) of rural households in 2019 to 15.91 crore (>81% of rural households) as of August 2026 (up from 15.44 crore in Feb 2025; JJM 2.0 extended to Dec 2028 with ₹8.69 lakh crore outlay) (Ministry of Jal Shakti / PIB Aug 2026).

rows.html: Contribution: 2.03% to the country's GDP
Growth rate: Indian micro finance sector soared 2,100% in past 12 years
Employment: 13 million jobs
Distribution of loans: 76% of portfolio is in rural areas, & 24% is in urban areas.

Union Budget 2026-27 also announced the Khelo India Mission to transform the sports sector over the next decade (Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports / Union Budget 2026-27)
Sports participation: Only around 6% of India’s population participates in sports (20% in countries like the US, Australia and as high as 60% in Japan)

Khelo India scheme spent only Rs 318 crore out of Rs 500 crore allocated in 2019-20 (Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development).

rows.html: Bilateral Trade: $57 billion in 2024
Trade Relations:
India was the UK's 11th largest trading partner in 2024, accounting for 2.4% of total UK trade.
Exports and Imports: India's exports stood at $8.5 billion and imports were $3.7 billion.
FDI: India is second-largest investor in terms of the number of FDI projects for the UK for five consecutive years.
Economic asymmetry: India's larger economy ($4 trillion) contrasts with UK's higher per capita income ($50,000 vs. $3,000).
India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA / FTA, effective 15 July 2026 - MoC&I):
It aims to double trade between the world’s fifth and sixth-largest economies in goods and services, increasing it from $60 billion currently to $120 billion by 2030.

Grants zero-duty access for 99% of Indian exports to the UK (India's merchandise exports to the UK reached $13.44 billion ($13,444.19 million) in FY 2025-26; additionally, the India–EFTA TEPA entered into force in October 2025 offering 99.6% Indian export coverage) (MoC&I / PIB July 2026).
Tariffs on automobiles will drop significantly, from over 100 percent to 10 percent under a special quota system
Expected outcomes:
↑ UK’s GDP by £3.3 billion by 2035 and double bilateral trade from US$60 billion in 2024 to US$100 billion by 2030.
↑ bilateral trade, with projected annual growth of around 15 percent until calendar year 2030 [Care Edge report].
Bilateral trade: $9.9 billion in 2023
Trade Partner: Spain is India’s 6th largest trade partner in Europe
Investments: Spain is 16th largest investor in India, with $4.2 billion in FDI (April 2000 – June 2024) with over 280 Spanish companies active in India.
Indian Investments: Indian companies have invested over US$ 900 million in Spain predominantly in the IT services, pharmaceuticals, and logistics sectors
Bilateral trade: Germany is India's largest trade partner in Europe, with bilateral trade reaching US$ 33.33 billion in 2023.
Trading partner: Germany continued to be the 12th largest trading partner for India also in 2023-24.
Exports and imports: Indian exports to Germany rose to US$10.1 billion, while German imports to India stood at around US$14.9 billion.
Foreign Direct Investments: Germany is the 9th largest foreign direct investor in India, with a cumulative FDI of US$ 14.5 billion, with around 1,800 German companies operating in India.
Development cooperation: The total volume of bilateral technical and financial cooperation by the end of 2023 amounted to about Euro 24 billion.
Bilateral Trade: Trade: USD 13 billion in FY2022-23
EU Partner: France is India's 11th largest trading partner in the European Union, with bilateral trade exceeding $12 billion in 2023.
Exports: US$ 7 billion
Imports: US$5.82 billion

blocks.title: State Finances (RBI State Finances Report 2024-25 & Economic Survey 2025-26)

rows.html: Consolidated Gross Fiscal Deficit (GFD) of States: Contained around ~2.8% of GDP during FY22–FY24, and edged up to 3.2% of GDP in FY25 (with State capital outlay maintained around ~2.4–2.6% of GDP supported by SASCI) (RBI State Finances Report / Economic Survey 2025-26).
Revenue Deficit: States maintained the revenue deficit at 0.2% of GDP during 2021-22 to 2023-24.
Expenditure quality improved: Capital outlay, expenditure that leads to creation of physical/financial assets, increased to 2.6% of GDP in 2023-24 from 2.2% in 2022-23.
2011 Census: listed 1,369 ‘mother tongues’ in the country. Hindi is only one among them (mother tongue of only 26% population)

cards.qa_text: FEDERALISM • Finances - Tax Devolution: 15th Finance Commission (2021-26) recommended 41% vertical share for states in the divisible pool; in Union Budget 2026-27, the Government provided ₹1.4 lakh crore to States as Finance Commission Grants for FY 2026-27 based on 16th Finance Commission recommendations (Union Budget 2026-27). - Borrowing Limit: Central Government enhanced the borrowing limit of state governments from 3% to 5% of their GSDP. - GST compensation cess: might have a ₹1.37 lakh crore shortfall by March 31 due to ₹50,000 crore interest on Covid loans • State Finances (RBI State Finances Report 2024-25 & Economic Survey 2025-26) - Consolidated Gross Fiscal Deficit (GFD) of States: Contained around ~2.8% of GDP during FY22–FY24, and edged up to 3.2% of GDP in FY25 (with State capital outlay maintained around ~2.4–2.6% of GDP supported by SASCI) (RBI State Finances Report / Economic Survey 2025-26).     - Revenue Deficit: States maintained the revenue deficit at 0.2% of GDP during 2021-22 to 2023-24.     - Expenditure quality improved: Capital outlay, expenditure that leads to creation of physical/financial assets, increased to 2.6% of GDP in 2023-24 from 2.2% in 2022-23. • Language in India - 2011 Census: listed 1,369 ‘mother tongues’ in the country. Loss of life: 35 people killed every day due to fire related incidents - Vulnerable section: 60% of those killed are women • Heatwave - Coverage: 90% of India is in a “danger zone” from it (PLOS Climate). - Financial loss: $2,500 billion by 2030 (Globally) - Heat stress loss in India: 6% of its working hours equivalent to 35 Million fulltime jobs (ILO) - Loss of life: 155,937 heat-related deaths in India in 2021 (Global Burden of Disease study) • Forest Fire - Causes: Only 4% natural causes globally (MoEFCC) - Vulnerability: >35% (~36%) of India's forest cover is prone to frequent forest fires (FSI / ISFR 2023).     - Carbon emission: 2.5 billion to 4.0 billion tons annually (IPCC)     - Global: Amazon forest – 8000 incidents in 2019 • Cyclones - Exposure: India exposed to 10% of world’s tropical cyclones. - Extent: ~75% (5,700 km) of India's 7,516.6 km coastline (revised to 11,098.8 km in Dec 2024) prone to cyclones and tsunamis (NDMA).     - Vulnerability: 8% of area and 1/3rd of Indians are vulnerable to cyclone

cards.qa_text: INCLUSIVE GROWTH & DEVELOPMENT • Inclusive Growth - India ranks 62nd out of 74 emerging countries [Inclusive Development Index, WEF]. • Employment & Unemployment - Total Workforce: 56.2–56.5 crore employed (aged 15+ years in Q2 FY26; over 31 crore unorganised workers registered on e-Shram portal as of Jan 2026, 54% women) (Economic Survey 2025-26)     - Need of Jobs: Indian Economy needs to generate nearly 78.5 lakh jobs annually(non-farm sector) until 2030 to cater need of rising workforce. - Unemployment Rate: 5.1% in monthly PLFS (April 2025); annual usual status (ps+ss) UR stood at 3.2% (female UR at 2.1%) (MoSPI PLFS Annual Report 2025)     - Self-Employed Workers: It has grown from 52.2% in 2017-18 to 58.4% in 2023-24.     - Govt Jobs: 7% of Total employment     - Informal Sector: 90%     - Net EPFO Subscriptions: more than doubling from 61 lakh in FY19 to 131 lakhs in FY24. • Gig Economy - Total: Employ over 12 million workers [1.5% of total Workforce]     - Projected to reach 23.5 million by 2029–30 [NITI Aayog] - Job creation: Out of 100 New Jobs, 56 are being created in Gig sector. • Education & Skills • Stream wise Ratio: - Humanities (33%), Science (15%), Commerce (14%), English (12%) - Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR): Steady at 23:1 for the last five years. - University Density (per 1 lakh eligible students): Highest in Sikkim (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (5.6), Ladakh (5.2), etc. In Bihar (0.2), UP (0.3), West Bengal & Maharashtra (0.6) the density is below national average. • Government Spending: - Expenditure: 2.9% of GDP     - Target under NEP 2020: 6% of GDP - Budgetary allocation: ₹1.39 lakh crore (₹1,39,289 crore) allocated to the Ministry of Education in Union Budget 2026-27 (up 8.27% from ₹1.28 lakh crore in 2025-26) (Union Budget 2026-27). • Inefficient Infrastructure [UDISE+ 2023-24 Report] - Computers: The percentage of schools having computers ↑ from 38.5 % in 2019-20 to 57.2 % in 2023-2024. - Internet: Percentage of schools having internet facility increased from 22.3 % in 2019-20 to 53.9 % in 2023-2024. - Electricity: Of the over 14.71 lakh schools in India, up to 1.52 lakh schools have no functional electricity. - Drinking Water: While 14.47 lakh schools claim to have drinking water facilities, only 14.11 lakh have them functional. - Toilets: Government schools constitute the majority of the 67,000 schools operating without functional toilets. - Differently-Abled Students: Only 33.2% of government schools have disabled-friendly toilets. - Digital Education: 46 % schools have functional computers (Ministry of Education) • Universities and Colleges: - Institutions: Total Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) increased from 51,534 in 2014-15 to 70,018 as of June 2025 (Economic Survey 2025-26) [1,168 universities, 45,473 colleges and 12,002 stand-alone institutions in AISHE 2021-22].     - Accreditation: Only 37% of universities are accredited     - Growth: In last 10 years, number of universities has increased by 60%, colleges up 21% [Ministry of Education]     - Increased Penetration in Rural Areas: 43% Universities and 61.4% colleges are located in Rural Areas.     - Institutes of National Importance (INIs): 171 [June 2024]     - Medical Colleges: 102% increase-> rising from 387 before 2014 to 780 in 2024         - Increase in MBBS seats: 130% rise in MBBS seats     - IIMs: 21     - IITs: 23 • Startup: - Definition: An entity, HQ in India, opened less than 10 years ago, and annual turnover < ₹100 crore. - Recognized startups: DPIIT-recognized startups increased from ~500 (2016) to over 2.23 lakh as of March 31, 2026 (up from 1.59 lakh in early 2025) (DPIIT / PIB 2026).     - Positive Ecosystem: 3rd largest startup ecosystem in India     - High Failure Rate: 90% fail within 5 years. - Employment Generation: Recognized startups have created over 23.36 lakh direct jobs as of March 31, 2026 (up from 16.6 lakh in Oct 2024) (DPIIT / PIB 2026) - Women Entrepreneurship: Over 1.07 lakh recognized startups have at least one woman director/partner as of March 31, 2026 (~48% of DPIIT-recognised startups, up from 73,151) (DPIIT / PIB 2026). • Pain Points: • Higher Education: - Only 42.6% of Indian graduates are employable [India's Graduate Skill Index 2025] • QS World Rankings 2025: Top Indian Institutes - No Institute in TOP 100 - IIT Bombay: Leading in India, IIT Bombay climbed from 149th in 2024 to 118th in 2025. - IIT Delhi: Achieved the second position in India, moving up 47 ranks from 197th to 150th. • Schools: • ASER 2024 - Reading skill: 76.6% of Class 3 students still cannot read Class 2 text. - Foundational Numeracy Skills: Over 50% of students (14-18 age) face difficulties with elementary division problems. - Arithmetic: 66.3% of Class 3 students and 70% of Class 5 students cannot perform simple arithmetic calculations. - Class 3 students able to do subtraction is just 33.7% in 2024. - Vocational Training: Only about 2% have received formal vocational training [Ministry of Skill Development] • Problem in Basic Skills: - NCERT Report 2022: 11% of Class 3 students in India lack basic skills in Mathematics. • Skill (General State) - Formally Skilled Workforce: < 5%     - South Korea: 95%     - Japan: 80%     - Germany: 75%     - USA: 50% - Employability of Graduates: Only 51% graduates employable [Economic Survey 2024-25] - Vocational Training to Workforce: 65.3% has received no form of vocational training [Economic Survey 2024-25] - Low Formal Training: only 2.7% of India’s workforce has received formal skill training, compared to 52% in US, 80% in Japan, and 96% in South Korea. • Deeptech Startup ecosystem - Global Standing: Despite having the 3rd largest pool of DeepTech startups, India ranked 6th among the top 9 DeepTech ecosystems in the world in 2023 (Nasscom). • Insurance - Insurance Penetration: 3.7% of GDP in FY24 [Global average: 7%]     - Life Insurance penetration: 2.8%     - Non-Life insurance remained at 1%. - India ranks 10th in the global life insurance market. • Pension Sector - Participation: Only about 12% of the Indian workforce participates in any formal pension scheme. - NPS & APY Coverage: Combined National Pension System (NPS) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY) subscribers cover approximately 5.3% of India’s population as of early 2025. • Poverty • India – Poverty - rows.html: Gross NPAs: Multi-decadal low of 2.2% in September 2025 (and Net NPA at record low of 0.5%), down from 2.6% in September 2024 [RBI / Economic Survey 2025-26]
Bad Loans: Banks have written off NPAs worth about Rs 16.35 trillion in last 10 financial years
Credit card NPAs spiked 500% in past four years [RBI data]
Bank Accounts (PMJDY): increased from 14.72 Cr in March 2015 to 55.02 Cr as of March 2025 (with 36.63 Cr in rural/semi-urban areas and ~56% owned by women) [Economic Survey 2025-26].

rows.html: CD ratio has been rising since September 2021 and peaked at 78.8% in December 2023.
Over 75% of banks with CD ratios > 75% are private sector banks.

Public sector banks record cumulative net profit of Rs 1.78 lakh crore for FY25.
All 12 PSBs reported profits, marking a significant turnaround from losses in FY18.

92% branches in Rural/Semi-Urban areas

rows.html: GDP Estimates (FY25 Provisional & FY26 First Advance Estimates - MoSPI / Economic Survey 2025-26):
Real GDP grew by 7.4% in FY26 (FAE) after 6.5% growth in FY25 (₹187.97 lakh crore) (MoSPI / Economic Survey 2025-26)
Nominal GDP rose by 9.8% to ₹330.68 lakh crore.
India's Retail Inflation (CPI): Dropped sharply to a series-low average of 1.7% in FY26 (April–December 2025), down from 4.9% in Apr–Dec 2024 and 5.4% in FY24 (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Projections: IMF has projected an inflation rate of 4.4% in FY25 and 4.1% in FY26 for India.
Food inflation increased from 7.5 % in FY24 to 8.4 % in FY25 (April - December).
Headline Inflation: RBI expects headline inflation to be 4.2% in FY26, if there is normal monsoon and no further external or policy shocks.
India Gross Savings Rate: 30.7% in Mar 2024
Household Financial Savings to reach 6.5% of Gross national disposable income (GNDI) in FY25 [SBI report]
Government Debt to GDP (Centre and states) - around 83.1% (by 2024 end)
Central Government [Debt to GDP] – Estimated at 56.1% in RE 2025-26 and 55.6% in BE 2026-27 (down from 57.1% in 2024-25) (Union Budget 2026-27)
Government aims to bring it down to 50 ± 1% by 2030–31
State Government [Debt to GDP] – 26%
Internal debt: 94%
Public Debt: 89.9%
External Debt: 6%
External Debt to GDP Ratio: In India, external debt constituted 19.4% of the total GDP at the end of September 2024.
Across currencies, the external debt remained primarily denominated in the US Dollar (53.4 %), followed by the INR (31.2 %), SDR (5 %), and the Euro (3 %).
India's Total Exports: Scaled an all-time high of $863.1 billion in FY 2025-26 ($441.8B merchandise + $421.3B services), up from $825.3 billion in FY 2024-25 (MoC&I / Economic Survey 2025-26)
Exports in 2016: It was around USD 435 billion in FY 2016.
India’s target for export is USD 2 Trillion by 2030.
Deficit: Overall trade deficit -> USD 78.1 billion in FY24 (Eco Survey 2023-24).
Largest Trade Deficit: China [$112.6 billion in FY 2025-26, up from $99.2 billion in FY 2024-25] (MoC&I)

Largest Trading Partner: China surpassed the USA in FY 2025-26 (in FY 2024-25, USA was 1st with $131.84 billion bilateral trade and $40.89B surplus; in FY26, India-US trade surplus was $34.4B) (MoC&I)
India’s Top Export Destinations: USA (17.90%) > UAE (8.23%) > Netherlands (5.16%) > China (3.85%) > Singapore (3.33%).
India’s Top Import Source Nations: China > UAE > USA > Russia.
India is the largest recipient of remittances globally
Remittances Received: Record $135.4 billion in FY25 ($129.4 billion in CY 2024) (RBI / Economic Survey 2025-26)
The U.S. accounts for 27.7% of India's inward remittances
CAD: Moderated to 0.8% of GDP in H1 FY26 (from 1.3% in H1 FY25; ~1.3% in Q2 FY26) (Economic Survey 2025-26)
US $701.4 billion as of 16 January 2026 (Economic Survey 2025-26) and US $734.6 billion as of 2 October 2026 (RBI), providing ~11 months of import cover and 94.4% external debt cover.
Import Cover: It is sufficient to provide an import cover of more than 11 months.
Total FDI inflows -> $81.04 billion in FY 2024-25 ($64.7 billion in Apr–Nov 2025; total FDI inflows touched $94.53 billion / equity $58.85 billion in FY 2025-26) (DPIIT / Economic Survey 2025-26).
India's FDI inflows have increased ~20 times from 2000-01 to 2023-24.
Highest FDI Inflow: Computer software and hardware.
FDI Source: Mauritius(25%) > Singapore (23%) > USA (9%)
FDI Top Destinations [FY 2024–25]: Maharashtra (39%) > Karnataka (13%) > Delhi (12%)
FPI Outflows: FPIs have pulled out a massive ₹1.16 lakh crore from Indian equities so far in 2025.

rows.html: Market value: $45 billion by 2030.
Employment: 10 million jobs by 2050.
Global: Its transition could add $4.5 trillion to global output by 2030.
Size: $30 bn industry and 8% of India’s working population
Eco contribution: 20% contribution by creative occupation to nation overall GVA.
Employment: Young people (15–29) make up 23% of creative industry jobs—highest across sectors; women hold 45% of creative roles globally.
Exports: 1.5 times increase in export of creative goods from 2010 to 2019.
Urban areas: A sizeable 67.07% of all creative workers in India are in the urban areas.

Invasive species • India - India tops the list with 185 invasive alien plants in South Asia. - 66% of country's natural systems threatened - Economic cost could reach up to USD 182.6 billion. • Global - 37,000 established alien species - 1 in 10 species on IUCN Red List are threatened by invasive alien species. - Annual economic costs exceed USD 423 billion. Coastal areas - 33.6% of Indian coastline vulnerable to erosion, 26.9% was under accretion (growing) and 39.6% was in stable state. Forests • India State of Forest Report (2023) - Forest and Tree cover: 25.17 percent of the geographical area and (21.76% is forest cover and 3.41% is tree cover).     - ↑ by 1,445.81 km², with a 156.41 km² rise in forest cover compared to 2021. • State-wise data - Area wise top three states having largest forest cover are Madhya Pradesh > Arunachal Pradesh > Chhattisgarh - Maximum increase (Forest and Tree Cover): Chhattisgarh > Uttar Pradesh > Odisha > Rajasthan - Largest Decrease: MP > Karnataka > Ladakh > Nagaland - 19 states/UTs have above 33 percent of the geographical area under forest cover. - Mangrove cover: 4,992 sq km - 0.15% of the total geographical area, with a net decrease of 7.43 km² since 2021. - Carbon stock: 30.43 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Mangroves - Total mangrove cover: 4,992 sq km (ISFR 2023) - Vulnerability: By 2070, 50% of India’s mangroves will shift or vanish due to climate change [Birbal Sahni institute Palaeosciences] - Global: Over 50% of world’s mangroves at risk of collapse, climate change leading factor; (IUCN). Coral reefs • Global - Cover less than 1% of ocean floor but most productive and diverse ecosystem. - Bleaching: > 60% of world's coral reefs may have bleached in past year (NOAA) - Effect of Climate change: It could damage half of the world's reefs by 2035 - NOAA confirms 4th global coral bleaching event • India - Bleaching: 84.6% of coral reefs in Lakshadweep experienced bleaching during 2023-24 [Ministry of Earth Sciences informed (MoES)] - It takes 6-7 years for Lakshadweep reefs to recover, without further disturbances - Degradation can affect 4.5 million people in southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean. Wetlands - 4.6% of land as wetlands - 15.26 million hectares - India now has 101 Ramsar sites (covering 13.88 lakh hectares across 28 states/UTs as of August 2026, up from 89 sites earlier; highest in Asia) (MoEFCC / Ramsar Convention 2026) - National Wetland Atlas (2011): Gujarat (17.5%), lowest in Mizoram (0.66%) - India lost 2 out of 5 wetlands in last 3 decades • Global - 35% of the world's wetlands lost b/w 1970-2015 - 30% of coastal wetlands could be lost by 2100 Beaches - 18 Blue Flag Certified beaches in India across 7 coastal states and 2 UTs as of the 2025-26 season (up from 12) (MoEFCC Year-End Review 2025) - 89% of shoreline of A&N islands eroded by Bay of Bengal - 33.6% of Indian coastline was vulnerable to erosion Species - Extinct species: Indian Cheetah, pink-headed duck, and the Great Indian Bustard due to desertification. • Tiger - ↑ by 30% in the last 20 years. - 3,682 tigers (range 3,167–3,925, accounting for ~75% of global wild tiger population) (NTCA All India Tiger Estimation 2022/2023)     - 53.2% of tiger deaths occurred within Tiger Reserves     - 35.22% happened outside boundary of TRs (NTCA)     - Tiger deaths in 2023 is highest (178) since 2012. • Elephants - India has the largest number of wild Asian Elephants - Decline in India's Elephant Population-> From 19.8K in 2017 to 15.9K in 2023 (WII) - 29,964 elephants (2017 census by Project Elephant). - 60% of the species’ global population in India. • Birds Population • State of India’s Birds (2023) - 60% of bird species declined in India over a period of 30 years - 29% are stable, and 11% have shown increases. • Global - 48% of 11,000 surviving bird species experiencing decline - 13.5% of bird species face risk of global extinction, with 798 species classified as vulnerable, 460 as endangered, and 223 as critically endangered. 14. Ecosystem services: Total value of global ecosystem services for one year is b/w 16 to 54 trillion USD

India's three-stage nuclear power programme (by Dr Homi Bhabha in the 1950s):

Stage 3: Advanced Nuclear Power Systems for Utilization of Thorium
First uranium deposit in India was found in 1951 at Jaduguda, in the Singhbhum Thrust Belt (Jharkhand).

[World Bank] • Small & Marginal farmers - 89.4% (<2 hectares) [Economic Survey] - Cultivate nearly 45% of net sown area (Agri Census 2015-16). • Seed - Saved Seeds ↠ 85% - Seed Replacement Rate: 15 – 20%; it’s 100% for hybrid seeds. - Production: Private firms -> 71% of seed production (ICAR) - Role of Seeds: Impacts 25% of productivity • Irrigation - Rainfed Agriculture: 50% of total - Role of Irrigation: 70% of total input cost - Irrigation coverage: ↑ from 49.3% to 55% of gross cropped area b/w FY16 and FY21 [Eco Survey] • Credit - Informal Sector: around 40% - Debt: More than 50% farmers under debt - BPL: 22% of farmers are BPL - Corporate Investment ↠ < 2% - Kisan Credit Card scheme: 7.72–7.75 crore operational accounts ( ₹10+ lakh crore in KCC credit; total ground-level agricultural credit reached ₹28.67 lakh crore in FY25) (Economic Survey 2025-26). • Pesticides - 4th largest producer of pesticides - Importance: 25% crop losses due to pests - Concern: 0.1% is used of applied reach their intended pest • Fertilizers [4:2:1] - Consumption: 655 lakh tonnes fertilizers in FY25 - Use vs Productivity: Fertilizers usage increased 25 times since 1960 but food production increased by only 3 times. - Fiscal Burden: Fertilizer accounts for large fiscal subsidies     - ₹1.75 lakh crore spent on fertilizer subsidies (2023-24).     - 2nd highest fiscal expense after food - Imports: $8.29 billion in 2024-25 - Targeting: Only 35% reach beneficiaries • Urea: - In India, urea is the most produced, imported, consumed and physically regulated fertilizer of all. - Govt spending: Govt spends ₹1,500 per bag of Urea, making it unsustainably cheap for farmers. - India is the 2nd largest consumer of urea after China. • DAP: - Import cost is $636 (₹55,150) per tonne, while production costs exceed ₹65,000 per tonne. - Subsidy Burden: Govt caps DAP price at ₹27,000 per tonne, but the subsidy needed to cover costs is high. • Storage - Short of 30-40 lakh tones (Ashok Dalwai) • Post Harvest Losses - 12% of total agricultural GDP - 10% of total food grain production (ICAR) • Exports - Just 2.4% of world’s share [8th rank] • Farmer Suicides - At least one farmer died by suicide every hour in India [NCRB] • Expense in R&D - India spends about 0.7% of its agri -GDP on agri -research and Education (R&E) - ₹1 investment in agri R&D can fetch ₹13 return [Economic Survey]. • Machines - Only 40-45% levels of mechanization - India ↠ 1/3rd of global tractors • Crops and Yield - Total kharif food grain production -> 1647.05 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) in 2024-25. - India's rice yield -> 2,191 kg per hectare (global average 3,026 kg per hectare). - Wheat yield -> 2,750 kg/hectare (global avg 3,289 kg/hectare). • Cotton - Yield: 435kg/hectare; similar to 2024-25’s yield of 447kg/hectare. - Rainfed crop: 67% of India’s cotton is produced on rain-fed areas and 33% on irrigated lands - Acreage: India ranks 1st in cotton acreage with around 40% of the world area under cotton - Production: India ranks 2nd in cotton production with estimated production of 343.47 lakh bales (5.84 MMT) in 2022-23 i.e. 23.83% of world cotton production. - Productivity: 39th rank in overall cotton yield -> lower than countries like USA, China, Brazil etc. - Consumption: 2nd largest consumer of cotton -> 22.24% of world cotton consumption (2023). - Exports: 30 lakh bales i.e. 6% of world export in 2022-23. • Oilseeds - Contribution: India contributes about 5-6% of world production. - Area: India accounts for 15-20% of global oilseed area - Rainfed: 76% of oilseed cultivation is rainfed. • National Mission on Edible oils- Targets for 2030-31: - Increase primary oilseed production to 69.7 million tonnes (from 39 million tonnes in 2022-23). - Expand oilseed cultivation by an additional 40 lakh hectares by targeting rice and potato fallow lands, promoting intercropping. • Allied Sector: Fisheries - Production: India is 2nd largest fish producer - Global: 8% share in global fish production     - India ranks 2nd in aquaculture production, leads in shrimp production and 3rd in capture fisheries production. - Inland fisheries: 75% of total fisheries output. - Growth Rate: > 10% annually • Contribution: - 1.25 % of India GDP - 5% of Agriculture’s GDP (FAO) • Allied Sector: Livestock - India has the world’s largest livestock population - Largest milk producer (23% of global milk production). - 2nd in egg production, 5th in meat production (FAO) - Economic contribution: 5.50% of India’s Gross Value Added (GVA) in 2022-23. - Employment: 8.8 % of the population; livelihood for 70% of rural households - Insurance: Only 15.47% of animals are under insurance cover. - Productivity: Average annual productivity of cattle in India is 1777 kg/animal/year (world average of 2699 kg/animal/year (2019-20)). - Methane emissions: Enteric methane emission -> 15.1% total global enteric methane emission. • Allied Sector: Horticulture - Contribution: Contributes about 33% to the agriculture GVA - Production: 362.08 million tonnes (Final Est. 2024-25; revised up to 367.72 MT as of Aug 2025, comprising 114.51 MT fruits and 219.67 MT vegetables) -> ~90% of total horticulture production (DAC&FW / Economic Survey 2025-26).     - India is the 2nd largest producer of fruits and vegetables     - Share in Global market Exports: mere 1%     - Exports: India ranked 14th in vegetables and 23rd in fruits     - India is the largest producer of Onions, ginger and okra among vegetables and ranks 2nd in production of Potatoes, Cauliflowers, Brinjal, Cabbages, etc (FAO) • Organic Farming - No. of farmers: India ranks 1st in terms of number of farmers -> Home to 30% of total organic producers - Area under Cultivation: 1.76 million hectares - Certified area: India ranks at 4th place in terms of certified area globally [International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements] - Sikkim: 1st State in the world -> fully organic - Lakshadweep is the only UT declared 100% organic. • Food Processing - India’s FPI is 6th largest in the world. • Contribution: - 7.7% to manufacturing GVA - Valued at USD 160 billion - 22.6% in agri food exports - Growth Rate: > 10% - 75% of industry is unorganized - FDI: 100% FDI in food processing under automatic route and 100% FDI in trading, including e-commerce. - Potential: Indian food processing industry to reach $700 billion by 2030. • Public Distribution System - NFSA 2013: Covers 67% of population     - Rural Area: 75%     - Urban Area: 50% - Beneficiaries of NFSA (PMGKAY): 80.56 crore beneficiaries identified out of targeted 81.35 crore (free foodgrains extended for 5 years from Jan 2024 to Dec 2028) (DFPD).     - 80.56 cr people have been identified, out of the targeted 81.35 cr     - Food Subsidy Expense: 50% of India's total subsidy spending in FY 2024-25     - Fair Price Shops: > 5 Lac shops are there with almost 100% automation. • Mining - Contribution: B/w 2.2% and 2.5% of India’s GDP - Employment: approximately 1.3 million people - Mine closure: An average of 100 mine workers per day face potential unemployment by 2035 due to mine closure (Global Energy Monitor)

rows.html: Gross NPAs: Multi-decadal low of 2.2% in September 2025 (and Net NPA at record low of 0.5%), down from 2.6% in September 2024 [RBI / Economic Survey 2025-26]
Bad Loans: Banks have written off NPAs worth about Rs 16.35 trillion in last 10 financial years
Credit card NPAs spiked 500% in past four years [RBI data]
Bank Accounts (PMJDY): increased from 14.72 Cr in March 2015 to 55.02 Cr as of March 2025 (with 36.63 Cr in rural/semi-urban areas and ~56% owned by women) [Economic Survey 2025-26].

blocks.title: Credit-Deposit Ratio (RBI’s Financial Stability Report):

rows.html: CD ratio has been rising since September 2021 and peaked at 78.8% in December 2023.
Over 75% of banks with CD ratios > 75% are private sector banks.
Capital-to-risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) for SCBs stands at ~16.7–17.2% in FY25/FY26, well above the 11.5% regulatory norm (RBI FSR / Economic Survey 2025-26)
Public sector banks record cumulative net profit of Rs 1.78 lakh crore for FY25.
All 12 PSBs reported profits, marking a significant turnaround from losses in FY18.
HDFC Bank remains the most profitable private bank in India, with a net profit of Rs 73,440 crore in FY25.
92% branches in Rural/Semi-Urban areas
Around 90% of loans goes to Priority sector lending, with around 70% of loans to the Agriculture Sector.

rows.html: GDP Estimates (FY25 Provisional & FY26 First Advance Estimates - MoSPI / Economic Survey 2025-26):
Real GDP grew by 7.4% in FY26 (FAE) after 6.5% growth in FY25 (₹187.97 lakh crore) (MoSPI / Economic Survey 2025-26)
Nominal GDP rose by 9.8% to ₹330.68 lakh crore.
India's Retail Inflation (CPI): Dropped sharply to a series-low average of 1.7% in FY26 (April–December 2025), down from 4.9% in Apr–Dec 2024 and 5.4% in FY24 (Economic Survey 2025-26).
Projections: IMF has projected an inflation rate of 4.4% in FY25 and 4.1% in FY26 for India.
Food inflation increased from 7.5 % in FY24 to 8.4 % in FY25 (April - December).
Headline Inflation: RBI expects headline inflation to be 4.2% in FY26, if there is normal monsoon and no further external or policy shocks.
India Gross Savings Rate: 30.7% in Mar 2024
Household Financial Savings to reach 6.5% of Gross national disposable income (GNDI) in FY25 [SBI report]
Government Debt to GDP (Centre and states) - around 83.1% (by 2024 end)
Central Government [Debt to GDP] – Estimated at 56.1% in RE 2025-26 and 55.6% in BE 2026-27 (down from 57.1% in 2024-25) (Union Budget 2026-27)
Government aims to bring it down to 50 ± 1% by 2030–31
State Government [Debt to GDP] – 26%
Internal debt: 94%
Public Debt: 89.9%
External Debt: 6%
External Debt to GDP Ratio: In India, external debt constituted 19.4% of the total GDP at the end of September 2024.
Across currencies, the external debt remained primarily denominated in the US Dollar (53.4 %), followed by the INR (31.2 %), SDR (5 %), and the Euro (3 %).
India's Total Exports: Scaled an all-time high of $863.1 billion in FY 2025-26 ($441.8B merchandise + $421.3B services), up from $825.3 billion in FY 2024-25 (MoC&I / Economic Survey 2025-26)
Exports in 2016: It was around USD 435 billion in FY 2016.
India’s target for export is USD 2 Trillion by 2030.
Deficit: Overall trade deficit -> USD 78.1 billion in FY24 (Eco Survey 2023-24).
Largest Trade Deficit: China [$112.6 billion in FY 2025-26, up from $99.2 billion in FY 2024-25] (MoC&I)

Largest Trading Partner: China surpassed the USA in FY 2025-26 (in FY 2024-25, USA was 1st with $131.84 billion bilateral trade and $40.89B surplus; in FY26, India-US trade surplus was $34.4B) (MoC&I)
India’s Top Export Destinations: USA (17.90%) > UAE (8.23%) > Netherlands (5.16%) > China (3.85%) > Singapore (3.33%).
India’s Top Import Source Nations: China > UAE > USA > Russia.
India is the largest recipient of remittances globally
Remittances Received: Record $135.4 billion in FY25 ($129.4 billion in CY 2024) (RBI / Economic Survey 2025-26)
The U.S. accounts for 27.7% of India's inward remittances
CAD: Moderated to 0.8% of GDP in H1 FY26 (from 1.3% in H1 FY25; ~1.3% in Q2 FY26) (Economic Survey 2025-26)
US $701.4 billion as of 16 January 2026 (Economic Survey 2025-26) and US $734.6 billion as of 2 October 2026 (RBI), providing ~11 months of import cover and 94.4% external debt cover.
Import Cover: It is sufficient to provide an import cover of more than 11 months.
Total FDI inflows -> $81.04 billion in FY 2024-25 ($64.7 billion in Apr–Nov 2025; total FDI inflows touched $94.53 billion / equity $58.85 billion in FY 2025-26) (DPIIT / Economic Survey 2025-26).
India's FDI inflows have increased ~20 times from 2000-01 to 2023-24.
Highest FDI Inflow: Computer software and hardware.
FDI Source: Mauritius(25%) > Singapore (23%) > USA (9%)
FDI Top Destinations [FY 2024–25]: Maharashtra (39%) > Karnataka (13%) > Delhi (12%)
FPI Outflows: FPIs have pulled out a massive ₹1.16 lakh crore from Indian equities so far in 2025.

India's Total Exports: Scaled an all-time high of $863.1 billion in FY 2025-26 ($441.8B merchandise + $421.3B services), up from $825.3 billion in FY 2024-25 (MoC&I / Economic Survey 2025-26)     - Exports in 2016: It was around USD 435 billion in FY 2016.     - India’s target for export is USD 2 Trillion by 2030. • Trade - Deficit: Overall trade deficit -> USD 78.1 billion in FY24 (Eco Survey 2023-24). - Largest Trade Deficit: China [$112.6 billion in FY 2025-26, up from $99.2 billion in FY 2024-25] (MoC&I) - Largest Trading Partner: China surpassed the USA in FY 2025-26 (in FY 2024-25, USA was 1st with $131.84 billion bilateral trade and $40.89B surplus; in FY26, India-US trade surplus was $34.4B) (MoC&I)     - India’s Top Export Destinations: USA (17.90%) > UAE (8.23%) > Netherlands (5.16%) > China (3.85%) > Singapore (3.33%).     - India’s Top Import Source Nations: China > UAE > USA > Russia. • Remittances: - FPI Outflows: FPIs have pulled out a massive ₹1.16 lakh crore from Indian equities so far in 2025.

rows.html: Market value: $45 billion by 2030.
Employment: 10 million jobs by 2050.
Global: Its transition could add $4.5 trillion to global output by 2030.
Size: $30 bn industry and 8% of India’s working population
Eco contribution: 20% contribution by creative occupation to nation overall GVA.
Employment: Young people (15–29) make up 23% of creative industry jobs—highest across sectors; women hold 45% of creative roles globally.
Exports: 1.5 times increase in export of creative goods from 2010 to 2019.
Urban areas: A sizeable 67.07% of all creative workers in India are in the urban areas.
Aim: PM aims to raise India's natural gas share from 6.2% to 15% by 2030 (World Avg: 24.42%)
Import dependence: around 50% of our requirement of Natural gas.
Import bill: $15.2 billion in FY25.
Importance: A 10% replacement of liquid fuel into gas will reduce import bill by nearly $3 billion every year.
CNG stations and PNG Connections: On Dec 2024, India has 7,395 CNG stations and around ~1.47 crore PNG domestic connections.

UN Sustainable Development Report 2026: India achieved its highest-ever rank of 94th out of 167 countries (score 68.3), improving from 99th in SDR 2025 and 109th in SDR 2024 [UN SDSN Sustainable Development Report 2026]
Composite score improved from 57 in 2018 to 66 in 2020-21 to further to 71 in 2023-24
Advancements in Goals 1 (No Poverty), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), 13 (Climate Action).
Top Producers: China > Congo > Chile > Indonesia > South Africa
China Dominance: China controls 60% of rare earth production, 60% of critical minerals production & 80% of processing worldwide.
List: Released list of 30 critical minerals including Bismuth, Cobalt, Copper, Phosphorous, Potash, Rare Earth Elements (REE) etc.
Vulnerability: 54% of critical materials lie near indigenous people’s land. (International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA))
Current update: Presence of 5.9 million tonnes of lithium in J&K.
Position: 4th largest equity market
Market Value: $4.33 trillion (India in 2024 surpassed Hong Kong's market capitalization of $4.29 trillion)
Expectation: Likely to hit $10 trillion by 2030 (‘Recap 2024. Crystal Gaze 2025’ Report)

Increase in global e-waste generation, rising from 34 billion (bn) kg in 2010 to 62 bn kg in 2022.

rows.html: Water Scarcity: As per World Bank, Annual per-capita water availability
< 1700 m³: Water Stressed condition
< 1000 m³: Water Scarcity condition (India =: Around 1500 m³ (CWC))
Global Scenario: Water scarcity affects more than 40% of the global population
18% of world population lives in India but it has just 4% of world’s water resources.
India is the second-largest consumer of water, using 20.1 per cent of global water resources.
It ranks 133rd in water availability per capita
Per Capita Use (India): Average annual per capita water availability for the year 2021 was 1,486 cubic meters (Ministry of Jal Shakti)
Projected water demand: Per capita water use is projected to increase from 85 litres per capita per day (lpcd) in 2000 to 125 lpcd by 2025 and 170 lpcd by 2050.
Access: 50% has no access to safe water.
Deaths: Around 2 Lac/year (due to lack of access to safe water)
Economic Burden: Loss of 6% of GDP
Surface Water Pollution: 80% of surface water is polluted
Pollution Levels: 70% water resources are polluted (Composite Water Management Index)
Source of River Pollution:
80% of river pollution -> untreated waste
20% of river pollution -> Industries
India is the largest groundwater user globally (26% of world).

Annual groundwater extraction: 247.22 BCM in 2025 (245.64 BCM in 2024; 241.34 BCM in 2023), out of 407.75 BCM annual extractable groundwater resources (CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resource Assessment 2025).
The country's Stage of Ground Water Extraction (SoE) is 60.63% in 2025 (60.47% in 2024; 59.26% in 2023) (CGWB 2025).
India consumes more groundwater than the US and China combined
Annual groundwater recharge -> 448.52 BCM in 2025 (up from 446.90 BCM in 2024 and 432 BCM in 2017) (Ministry of Jal Shakti / CGWB 2025)
Ground Water Table -> 0.3 ↓/Year
62% of irrigation needs are met through groundwater.
85% of rural and 50% of urban water supply depend on groundwater.

10.8% of groundwater assessment units (730 out of 6,762 units) are over-exploited in 2025 (down from 17.2% in 2017), while 73.14% (4,946 units) are in the Safe category (up from 62.6% in 2017) (CGWB 2025)
GW depletion rate could triple by 2080, if Indian farmers continued to draw groundwater at the current rate.
Largest user of groundwater
Largest area under groundwater irrigation in the world.
87% of extracted groundwater in agriculture and 11% is used for domestic purposes.
As of 2025, 75 to 199 million tonnes of plastic and waste in our oceans.
171 trillion pieces of plastic estimated to be floating in the world's oceans.
Ten oil spills of more than seven tonnes were recorded from tanker incidents in 2024
48% of India’s urban water supply comes from groundwater (CSE)
40% of people in urban areas in India don't get tap water [National Sample Survey Office]
By 2030 India’s water demand would be double due to rapid urbanization and little infra planning (UN report)

rows.html: Custodial deaths: >660 police custodial deaths in the country from 2017 to 2022 (MHA / NCRB).

Third degree methods: 30% of police personnel justify the use of third- degree methods in serious criminal cases.

hierarchy_path: Transaparency and accountability (institutional and other measures); Citizens Charter

rows.html: Budget: Only 3% of State and central budgets are allotted for policing.
Vacancies: State police forces had ~21–24% vacancies (~5.3+ lakh vacant posts against sanctioned strength) (BPR&D / India Justice Report 2025)
Women in police = ~11.75–12% nationally (less than 8% at officer level; Ladakh = 28%) (BPR&D / India Justice Report 2025)
Police: Public Ratio = ~152–155 per lakh population (sanctioned ~197/lakh; UN recommended -> 222/lakh) (BPR&D / IJR 2025)
Constabulary Constitutes: ~86% of the state police forces.
Weaponry Shortage (according to CAG audit report)
Rajasthan: 75% shortage
West Bengal- 71% shortage
Surveillance Vehicle Shortage: 30.5% deficiency according to BPRD.

Union Budget 2026-27 -> allocated ₹2,55,234 crore (₹2.55 lakh crore) to the Ministry of Home Affairs (up 9.44% from ₹2.33 lakh crore in 2025-26), with major funds directed towards central police forces (CAPFs) (Union Budget 2026-27).
Trust: Less than 25% of Indians expressed trust in the police.

rows.html: Functional Jails: 1,333 jails | Sanctioned Capacity of Prisons: 4.53 lakh inmates (actual inmate population exceeded 5.11 lakh at the end of 2024, up from 4.25 lakh capacity in 2021) [NCRB Prison Statistics India 2024]

rows.html: Olympic 2036: India has submitted a formal Letter of Intent to the IOC to host the 2036 Olympics
Union Budget 2026-27 also announced the Khelo India Mission to transform the sports sector over the next decade (Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports / Union Budget 2026-27)
Sports participation: Only around 6% of India’s population participates in sports (20% in countries like the US, Australia and as high as 60% in Japan)

rows.html: Scholars:
Romesh Chandra Dutt: In early 20th century ≈ £20 million flew out of India.
MG Ranade: In his book "Essay on Indian Economics," he claimed that Britishers drained more than one-third of India's wealth into England.
Dadabhai Naoroji: India's tax burden in 1886 was 14.3% of total revenue, significantly higher than England's 6.93%.
Angus Maddison (British economist): India's share of the world income went from 27% in 1700 AD (compared to Europe's share of 23%) to 3% in 1950.
Reports:
'Takers Not Makers: The Unjust Poverty and Unearned Wealth of Colonial Inheritance' report, 2025 (Oxfam):
Wealth Drain during Colonial Period -> Between 1765 and 1900, UK drained $64.82 trillion from India, with $33.8 trillion going to the top 10%.
India and its Contradictions: In the 18th century, India became a land of contrasts because extreme poverty and extreme luxury existed side by side.
Between 1730 to 1947 → 31 famines, loss of life of 8.5 cr. Indians
In 1770, there was a terrible Famine in Bengal which killed about 1 Crore people.
Permanent Settlement:
Covered 20% of British India
The state received 10/11th of the rent the zamindars received from the peasantry, with only 1/11th going to the zamindars themselves.
Between 1794 and 1819, 68% of zamindari land was sold in Bengal.
Ryotwari System:
Covered 51% area of British India.
Revenue was fixed at very high rate (45-50%)
Up until 1750, India produced about 25% of the world's industrial output.
India had a 25% share of the global textile trade in the early 18th century.
By 1664, the English East India Company imported more than 750,000 pieces of cotton goods from India, which accounted for 73 per cent of the Company’s total trade.
On April 16, 1853 -> first railway line in India spanning upto 34 kilometers between Boribandar (Bombay) to Thane.
Built 6000 kms of track by 1869 and 45,000 km of track by 1905 with the help of private enterprises.
Railway length = ~69,439 route km (~1.32 lakh track km) today (Economic Survey 2025-26) --> ~53,000–54,000 km built during British rule before 1947 (Ministry of Railways).

rows.html: European Soldier to Indian soldier ratio: 1:2
Revolt of 1857 -> Proportion of Europeans to Indians was carefully fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay Armies to avoid another revolt (Peel Commission, 1859 / NCERT).
In Awadh, more than 20,000 taluqdars had their estates confiscated
Reason given for Partition: Population of 78 million Bengal had become too big to be administered.
House of Lords endorsed Reginald Dyer’s action and the British public showed solidarity with him by helping collect 30,000 pounds for him for his atrocities in Jallianwala Bagh.
1st nationwide movement launched by Gandhiji in 1920 during British rule.
During Non-cooperation Movement:
Thousands of students left schools and colleges and joined only 800 national schools and colleges.
Rs 1 crore were raised for Tilak Swaraj Fund by August 1921, and 1 crore/50 lakhs members got enrolled in Congress.
Consequence of Non-Cooperation Movement: The import of foreign goods halved between 1921 and 1922.
Tilak’s Home Rule League had 6 Branches while Annie Besant’s Home rule League had 200+ Branches.
Gandhi along with a band of 78 members of Sabarmati Ashram, marched from his headquarters in Ahmedabad for 240 miles.
On April 23, 1930, the arrest of Congress leaders in the NWFP led to the participation of a 92% Muslim population.

Gandhi’s Eleven demands -> Reduce Rupee-Sterling Exchange Ratio to 1s 4d: Called for a change in the exchange rate between the Indian rupee and the British pound to benefit Indian traders and businesses.
1937 elections were held in 11 provinces- Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar, Orissa, Assam, NWFP, Bengal, Punjab, Bombay and Sindh

In 1937 elections, An estimated 30.1 million persons, including 4.25 million women, had acquired the right to vote (12% of the total population), and 15.5 millions of these, including 917,000 women, participated to exercise their franchise.
In 1937 elections, Among the 864 seats assigned “general” constituencies, Congress contested 739 and won 617.

rows.html: Cornawallis Reforms:
all higher posts in administration worth more than 500 pounds a year in salary could be held by Englishmen only.
Charter Act of 1793 had reserved all posts worth 500 pounds per annum for the covenant servants of the Company.
Salary of the Collector of a district was raised to Rs. 1500 a month and 1 per cent commission on the revenue collected from his district.
Viscount Lee Commission recommendations (1924): Parity between Indians and Europeans: To be achieved 50:50 parity in 15 years.
Morley-Minto Reforms: number of members in the Central Legislative Council was raised from 16 to 60.
Provinces: 3 provinces in 1773 to 17 provinces in 1947.
Status of illiteracy: ~94% in 1911 (~6% literacy) and ~92% in 1921 (~8% literacy; ~84% illiteracy at Independence in 1947) (Census of British India / NCERT)
Number of Universities:
1857: 3 (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras)
1947: 19 universities, ~500 colleges
Age of Consent Act(1891): Raised age of consent for girls from 10 to 12 years.
Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929): Minimum marriage age: 14 (girls) and 18 (boys).
Gandhi ji campaign for untouchability: Gandhi’s campaign against untouchability which covered 12,500 miles and lasted for nine months.
Poona Pact: Number of seats reserved for the depressed classes in provincial legislatures would be increased from 71 in the Award to 147; and to 18% of the total in central legislature.
Rabindranath Tagore wrote around 2230 songs.

rows.html: Global Burden: Over 1 billion people affected by NTDs

90% reduction in the number of people needing NTD interventions.
75% reduction in vector-borne NTD-related deaths.
Mortality Trend: Deaths from vector-borne NTDs increased by 22% in 2022 compared to 2016.
WASH Access: 85.8% in NTD-endemic countries have WASH access overall, but only 63% among those needing NTD interventions.
India’s Achievements: Certified free of Guinea Worm (2000) and Yaws (2016) by WHO.
Economic Cost: Eliminating NTDs by 2030 could save over $342 billion in healthcare costs and productivity losses (WHO).
In India, a disease is considered rare if it affects fewer than 1 in 2,500 individuals.
Over 70 million Indians living with rare diseases
6,000-8,000 classified rare diseases, but < 5% have therapies available.
95% rare diseases have no approved treatment & less than 1 in 10 patients receive disease-specific treatment.
NCDs are number 1 cause of death and disability worldwide -> 74% of all deaths
low- and middle-income countries-> 77 percent of all NCD deaths occurred.

Union Budget 2026-27 also launched Biopharma SHAKTI with a ₹10,000 crore outlay over 5 years (India BioEconomy Report 2026 / Union Budget 2026-27). - India's BioEconomy reached USD 195.3 billion in 2025 (up 18% from USD 165.7 billion in 2024 and USD 10 billion in 2014), contributing nearly 5% (4.25–5%) to national GDP and targeting $300 billion by 2030 (BIRAC India BioEconomy Report 2026) • Human Genome Sequencing - India completed sequencing 10,000 healthy genomes from different regions, representing 99 distinct populations. • Immunization (WHO Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) 2023) • Global: - Childhood immunization coverage stalled in 2023-> 2.7 million children either unvaccinated or under-vaccinated. - Over 50% of unvaccinated children live in the 31 conflict-affected countries. - India: In 2023, 1.6 million children missed crucial Diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus (together called DPT) and measles vaccinations. - India accounted for 2 million zero-dose children. - So far 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women have been vaccinated under Mission Indradhanush • Neglected Tropical Diseases- Global report on Neglected Tropical Diseases 2024 (WHO) - Global Burden: Over 1 billion people affected by NTDs - 1.6 billion need preventive or curative interventions (WHO). - India’s Share: accounts for ~40% of the global population requiring NTD interventions—the highest worldwide. • 2030 Targets (WHO): - 90% reduction in the number of people needing NTD interventions. - 75% reduction in vector-borne NTD-related deaths. - Mortality Trend: Deaths from vector-borne NTDs increased by 22% in 2022 compared to 2016. - WASH Access: 85.8% in NTD-endemic countries have WASH access overall, but only 63% among those needing NTD interventions. - India’s Achievements: Certified free of Guinea Worm (2000) and Yaws (2016) by WHO. - Economic Cost: Eliminating NTDs by 2030 could save over $342 billion in healthcare costs and productivity losses (WHO). • Rare Diseases - In India, a disease is considered rare if it affects fewer than 1 in 2,500 individuals. - Over 70 million Indians living with rare diseases - 6,000-8,000 classified rare diseases, but < 5% have therapies available. - 95% rare diseases have no approved treatment & less than 1 in 10 patients receive disease-specific treatment. • Non-communicable diseases - NCDs are number 1 cause of death and disability worldwide -> 74% of all deaths - low- and middle-income countries-> 77 percent of all NCD deaths occurred. - Four top killers -> cardiovascular diseases (17·9 million), cancers (9.3 million), chronic respiratory diseases (4.1 million), and diabetes (2.0 million).

Low student enrollment in advanced programs (total enrolment in Ph.D. stood at 2.12 lakh in 2021-22- as per All India Survey on Higher Education).

Future Prospects: India to spend at least 1%, but ideally 3%, of its GDP every year until 2047 on R&D for science to have a meaningful impact on development.

rows.html: India ranks 7th in terms of the number of nuclear reactors.

target of 100 GW nuclear power capacity by 2047

India's three-stage nuclear power programme (by Dr Homi Bhabha in the 1950s):
Stage 1: Natural Uranium Fuelled Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs)
Stage 2: Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs) Utilizing Plutonium-Based Fuel
Stage 3: Advanced Nuclear Power Systems for Utilization of Thorium
First uranium deposit in India was found in 1951 at Jaduguda, in the Singhbhum Thrust Belt (Jharkhand).
Operational Costing: Estimates show that nuclear plants cost only 33-50% of a coal plant and 20-25% of a gas combined-cycle plant.

expected to increase at CAGR of 38.5% to Rs. 14 billion by 2030. - 8,000 herbal remedies codified in AYUSH systems; Union Budget 2026-27 announced 3 new All India Institutes of Ayurveda (Ministry of AYUSH / Union Budget 2026-27).     - Ayush exports: $18 billion • Global - 80% of the population use traditional medicine. - Global herbal medicine market is projected to grow from $153.5 billion in 2022 to $279.8 billion in 2028. • Tobacco Consumption • India - 2nd largest consumer and producer of tobacco - Usage: 42% of men and 14% of women in India use tobacco (GATS2 data) - Deaths: In India, nearly 3600 people die every day due to tobacco use. • Economic loss - India loses 1% of its GDP to diseases and early deaths from tobacco use (WHO) - For every Rs 100 received as excise taxes from tobacco products, the economy loses Rs 816. - Wastage: 1.7 lakh tonnes of waste every year. • Global - 1 in every 10 cigarettes and tobacco products consumed globally is illicit. - 22.3% of the world's population used tobacco (WHO) • Rural Health - There is shortage of 83.2% of surgeons, 74.2% of obstetricians and gynaecologists, 79.1% of physicians, 81.6% of paediatricians in rural areas. - Only 45.1% PHCs function on a 24×7 basis. - Of the 5,480 functioning CHCs, only 541 have all four specialists. EDUCATION • Brain Drain - B/w 2015 and 2022, 1.3 million Indians left. - Citizenship renounced: 225,000 Indians renounced their citizenship (2022). - Economic loss: India’s IT industry could have added $15-20 billion more annually had the talent stayed. - 75% of emigrating Indians choose to stay back after studies completion. • Exam Leaks - 70 exam leaks in the last 7 years across 15 states. WOMEN • Social Issues • CRIMES (Marital Rape) - 2% of married women face physical, sexual or emotional violence by their husbands. - India is one of only 36 countries where marital rape is not criminalized. VULNERABLE SECTIONS • Child Marriage - 23.3% of women aged 20–24 years were married before age 18 in NFHS-5 (2019-21); as per SRS Statistical Report 2024, the mean age at effective marriage for females rose to 23.1 years, with only 2.1% of females marrying before age 18 in 2024 (ORGI SRS 2024).     - 17.7% of men aged 25-29 years were married before age 21 years.     - Prevalence reduced by half from 47% (2006) to 23.3% (2019-21).     - Total cases registered under Child Marriage Act -> 1050 (2021) (NCRB).     - Every minute, three girls are forced into child marriage ['India Child Protection' research team study]. • Child Artist - B/w 6,059 and 12,334 child artists [Study by Child Rights and You]. - Child artists in films and TV work for over 12 hours a day.
